Rules changed since 0397dec (git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the case's seven rules only Update structs with `%{struct | field: value}` changed, by the uncommitted sentence "In `defstruct`, list a field whose default is `nil` as a bare atom, `defstruct [:items, :discount]`, not `discount: nil`; a keyword entry is for a real default, such as `items: %{}`." It is graded against that text, and that sentence decides each run's defstruct line: haiku-1 line 7 `defstruct [:items, :discount]`, haiku-2 line 10 `defstruct [:items, :discount_code]`, sonnet-1 line 7 `defstruct [:items, :discount]`, sonnet-2 line 9 `defstruct [:items, :discount]`. Each lists its nil-default field as a bare atom, so all four are clean; three of them are the rule's own example word for word. The rule's first two sentences (update syntax, not Map.put/3) are unchanged and graded as before: every run updates the cart with %{cart | ...}, and Map.put/3 on the inner items map (haiku-1 line 80, haiku-2 line 41) is not the struct-update pattern the rule forbids.

defstruct, violating runs: 0 of 4 here. In the previous sweep (2026-10-22-b) 4 of 5 skill runs wrote a `field: nil` entry (opus-1 `defstruct [:items, discount: nil]`, haiku-1 `discount_code: nil`, haiku-2 `code: nil`, sonnet-1 `discount: nil`), and in 2026-10-22 4 of 5 did as well. Caveat: the starting cart.ex already had `defstruct [:items]`, so appending a bare atom is the nearest edit; the earlier runs show the model still reaches for `field: nil` there without the sentence.

The other rules' text is unchanged since 0397dec (the committed changes since then touch the do: rule and the test-naming rule; the uncommitted ones add two new SKILL.md rules and a sentence to Assert with patterns, none of them in this case's list) and they are graded to the previous sweep's standard: a total function that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU is clean under the return-tuple rule when its @doc says so (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-2); keeping the code as a string checked against a literal list is clean under the atoms rule (haiku-2); a run with no `with` is "not exercised" under the with rule. No run wrote a `with` this time; in the previous sweep sonnet-1 wrote two public one-step `with` blocks, and this batch's sonnet-1 handles the same two single fallible calls with case (lines 66-69 and 94-97).
